subject: Re: Order form — revenue-neutrality credit & floor adjustment
messages:
From: Dana Collins <dana.collins@acme-analytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@acme-analytics.com; salesops@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2026-08-25T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed changes to pricing floors / request for revenue-neutrality mechanism

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for sending the updated order form. Our procurement and finance teams reviewed Exhibit A and flagged two items that need discussion before we can proceed to countersign: the hard minimum monthly floor and the lack of a mechanism to prevent material revenue shifts for the first 6 months after launch.

Specifically: 
- The current minimum (2,500,000 tokens) creates a high overage risk given our phased rollout.
- We need a revenue-neutrality or credit mechanism that protects Acme for the ramp without creating perverse incentives long-term.

Can Redwood propose language that: (1) limits fee exposure during the initial 3-month ramp, (2) allows a single true-up, and (3) includes a cap on any credits issued? Our finance team expects a documented calculation we can run in-house.

Attached is the order form we exported with basic annotations. We prefer to avoid a lengthy addendum if possible.

Best,
Dana
Dana Collins
Head of Procurement — Acme Analytics

Attachment: ACME_OrderForm_submitted_v2.pdf (annotated)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Dana Collins <dana.collins@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed changes to pricing floors / request for revenue-neutrality mechanism

Dana — really appreciate the quick read and the annotations. We're committed to a commercially reasonable approach that protects both sides while preserving predictable unit economics. 

High-level proposal (first pass):
- Ramp window: 90-day ramp starting at contract effective date. During ramp, monthly floor reduced to 50% of Exhibit A floor.
- Revenue-neutrality credit: If actual monthly usage (tokens billed) during ramp is < 70% of the reduced floor, Redwood will issue a one-time deferred credit equal to the delta (floor — billed) * blended rate.
- Credit cap: credits limited to 20% of the total monthly invoice for any given month; aggregate credits capped at 10% of the first 12 months' committed spend.
- True-up: single true-up at day 120 (to reconcile ramp months).

We attached a redline of the Order Form that inserts the language above and a short worked example calculation (tab 2 in the MAP). Marissa looped in to confirm commercial/ops guardrails; Rishi is cc'd for finance visibility.

If this is directionally acceptable, our legal team will produce formal redlines for Acme to review. Otherwise call me and we can walk through quick scenarios.

Cheers,
Sooj
Soojjin (Sooj) Lee
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

Attachments: RW_OrderForm_redline_v1.pdf (proposed language + example), Mutual_Action_Plan_ACME-1147.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Dana Collins <dana.collins@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed changes to pricing floors / request for revenue-neutrality mechanism

Looping in a couple of legal/commercial clarifications so we get an executable redline next. Two points from our side: 
1) "Blended rate" above should be defined in Exhibit A (we suggest using the committed unit rates tiered by bucket in the Order Form; otherwise it becomes subjective).
2) We prefer a 15% per-month credit cap (instead of 20%) to align with our cost model; aggregate cap we suggested below to be conservative.

I've attached an internal legal markup (RW_Legal_Redline_v1.pdf) that applies the proposed language into the Order Form and a short paragraph that can be pasted into the main SOW/Exhibit B. If Acme wants an escrow-style reconciliation instead of a deferred credit, we can discuss but that requires procurement/legal approvals and adds execution friction.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: RW_Legal_Redline_v1.pdf (internal)

From: Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@acme-analytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Collins <dana.collins@acme-analytics.com>, finance@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2026-08-27T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed changes to pricing floors / request for revenue-neutrality mechanism

Soojin / Marissa — thanks for the quick response and the proposed language. A few items from Acme legal/finance that need clearer treatment before we can move forward: 

1) Definition of "ramp" — we need explicit start/stop triggers (e.g., first production inference request or date-of-first-invoice) and a fallback if we pause the rollout.
2) Credit mechanics — rather than an open-ended deferred credit, we prefer a mechanism where credits reduce future invoices with a clear expiry (e.g., credits must be applied within 12 months or forfeited). Also request a maximum monthly credit equal to 12% of the invoice to limit Redwood exposure.
3) Auditability — Acme needs the calculation to be auditable: token-level export for the ramp months and a sample verification workflow.

Inline comment: we are uncomfortable with a single true-up at day 120 if there are significant month-to-month fluctuations; would prefer a 60-day periodic true-up during the first 6 months.

Attaching our annotated comments to the order form. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to resolve quickly.

Regards,
Marcus Hale
Senior Counsel — Acme Analytics
marcus.hale@acme-analytics.com

Attachment: ACME_OrderForm_comments.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Hale <marcus.hale@acme-analytics.com>, Dana Collins <dana.collins@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed changes to pricing floors / request for revenue-neutrality mechanism

Marcus / Dana — thanks for the detailed notes and the auditability ask — totally reasonable. Proposed compromise below (redline language attached as RW_OrderForm_redline_v2):

- Ramp trigger: starts on date of first production inference request as recorded in our telemetry; if Acme pauses production for >30 consecutive days, ramp pauses and resumes on next production request.
- Ramp window: up to 90 days, with monthly checkpoints. If month N is under threshold, credit applies but is subject to monthly true-up at 60-day cadence for the first 6 months.
- Credit mechanics: deferred credits reduce future Redwood invoices and expire 12 months after issuance. Maximum monthly credit = 15% of that month's invoice; aggregate credit cap = 10% of first 12 months committed spend.
- Auditability: Redwood will provide token-level exports for ramp months (redacted PII) and a short verification report; Acme may request up to 2 sample verifications in the first 12 months.

If Acme accepts the above, next steps: 
1) Redwood legal will send RW_OrderForm_redline_v2 (attached) for Acme counsel to redline.
2) We will implement the MAP in the attached spreadsheet and request signature on the final order form + DocuSign link.

If you'd rather discuss by phone, I'm free 2–4pm PT tomorrow — otherwise we will push the redline and MAP to HubSpot and DocuSign.

Best,
Sooj
Soojjin Lee
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
